title: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy | Inside Rust Blog
excerpt: Want to follow along with Rust development? Curious how you might get involved? Take a look!
content_html:
Recently, five teams in the Rust project adopted a policy that I originally authored, governing how Large Language Models can be used when contributing to the rust-lang/rust monorepo. Notably, the new policy is not an official stance on LLMs, and does not apply everywhere in the Rust project. I wrote it for a very specific purpose, described below.

This post talks about why we created that policy, what it says, and how this will affect contributors.

The policy affects the following groups of people:

  • People who review or moderate PRs on rust-lang/rust.
  • People who author PRs with LLM-generated code on rust-lang/rust.
  • People who discover issues using LLMs and post them on rust-lang/rust.
  • People who write issues or comments that directly quote an LLM on rust-lang/rust.

If you are not in one of those groups, you don't have to change anything about how you work.

Why was this policy created?

While the Rust project is a collection of technical artifacts, it is also a community of people who work together to build, maintain, and extend those artifacts. When we talk about "contributing to the Rust project", we partly mean work on those artifacts, but we also mean joining that community and collaborating with the people already there.

Even before this policy was created, people were using LLMs to contribute to rust-lang/rust. Some of those uses respected our community: translating messages to English so people could draft them in their native language; finding poor diagnostics for code snippets that new contributors to Rust might write; analyzing RFCs to see if they were missing a discussion of other parts of the language that could affect the design. Some of those uses, sometimes unintentionally, did not.

I've seen LLMs causing three main issues for our community:

  1. Polished technical products no longer indicate effort and understanding.
  2. Making code easier to write exacerbates our existing issues with review bandwidth.
  3. People mechanically copy-pasting to and from an LLM is a waste of our time.

As time went on, these issues grew and grew, until we had to create dedicated channels and moderation policy for how to deal with them. However, those channels work against our goals of being transparent and welcoming, because new contributors have no idea what the rules are.

The new policy formalizes those rules publicly, so that new contributors know how to join our community without getting their PRs closed for reasons they don't understand, and so that existing reviewers can easily point to the rules as an actionable reason when closing PRs that don't follow them.

Technical products no longer indicate effort

It used to be that if an open source project got a polished, well-tested, detailed PR, that indicated that there was someone on the other end who had put time, effort, and understanding into the PR. That influenced Rust's culture in several ways:

  • We are generally reluctant to close PRs, since they represent someone else's hard work.
  • Our process emphasizes incremental discussions, where PRs are allowed to change existing design if we discover new facts during creation or review.
  • We treat PRs as an indication that someone is interested in joining our community and being mentored to work on future PRs.

With LLMs, none of these signals are reliable. Polished PRs no longer indicate effort; authors of polished PRs no longer necessarily understand their code—and in the case of autonomous agents, there is no longer someone on the other end at all; and because it's become so much easier to write code, a polished PR no longer indicates that someone is likely to stick around for the long term.

Making code easier to write causes review issues

At the time of writing, there are 1,281 open PRs to rust-lang/rust. This represents a staggering amount of time invested by both authors and reviewers. We have long had the problem that there are more people who want to write code than people willing to review it. With the advent of LLMs, this problem only gets worse.

Most of the work of reviewing is not simply catching bugs. A great deal of it is deciding whether this direction is a good approach, whether the PR is a good idea at all. In other words, reviewing is made of decisions.

"Shotgunning" PRs at reviewers incurs a high mental cost for them. I think most authors of LLM PRs believe that they are sincerely helping, but from our perspective, the code itself is the smallest and in some ways least important part of the change. We care much more about authors understanding what the code does, planning how it will change in the future, and deciding what it should look like. The code itself cannot help with any of those.

Mechanically copy-pasting LLM output is a waste of time

We will often get people who respond to review comments by copy-pasting them into their LLM, then copy-pasting its response back onto GitHub. Bluntly: this is a waste of everyone's time. If we wanted an LLM's opinion, we could have asked it ourselves. We want to hear your thoughts, not a machine's.

Moreover, this is a breach of trust between the reviewer and the author. Our assumption when we review is that we're talking to a real person who wants to do their best work. Pasting LLM text creates suspicion: does the author actually care? Is there a person here at all?

So why a policy?

Before this policy, we had a "wild west" approach to moderation. We had dozens of LLM PRs; no disclosure rules; people trying to add risky MIR optimizations as their first PR; and people posting "Verification: git diff --check" in their PR description as if that did something. While we had something for moderators to point to in the form of "Empower reviewers to reject burdensome PRs", our enforcement was inconsistent and our rules were not published anywhere. In practice, the rule was "anything goes, as long as it's not obviously horrible". Compared to the previous situation, the new policy is both much more strict and much more clear.

Regardless of your opinions on whether LLMs are good, bad, or a secret third thing, they can no longer be ignored. Our choices are not "no policy" or "policy". Our choice is whether to have the policy be an unofficial list of moderation notes or something we stand by publicly.

Why not ban LLMs altogether, or allow any use of LLMs that we think are pro-social? Because Rust governance doesn't work that way. We do not have a benevolent dictator who can say "No LLM-generated content, whether it be code or prose." or "AI is a tool, just like other tools we use".

Rust operates by consensus. As the policy says:

There is not a consensus within the Rust project—and likely never will be—about when/how/where it is acceptable to use AI-based tools. Many members of the Rust project and community find value in AI; many others feel that its negative impact on society and the climate are severe enough that no use is acceptable. Still others are working out their opinion.

Despite these differences, there are many values we all share:

  • Building a community of deep experts in our collective projects.
  • Building an inclusive community where all feel welcome and respected.

We want it to be possible to change the policy in the future. The policy has several provisions that make it easier to change than it was to originally adopt. The leadership council is also considering creating a sub-team that would handle LLM policy so we have fewer "nightmare" 30-person approval requirements.

I do not think every rule in this policy is wholly good. I do think that writing our rules down is better than not writing them down, and that having a policy that everyone kinda dislikes pushes us to improve our governance structures.

What does the policy say?

The policy summarizes itself this way:

It's fine to use LLMs to answer questions, analyze, distill, refine, check, suggest, review. But not to create.

Uses in the first category are allowed, sometimes requiring disclosure. Uses in the second category are heavily restricted.

General rules

No one except the author is required to read LLM output unless they choose to: LLM output isn't allowed in public docs, PR descriptions, or Github comments unless it's clearly marked; reviewers aren't required to look at LLM PRs if they don't want to.

No one is required to use LLMs to contribute to rust-lang/rust: policies must be written first for humans, and only summarized for machines; LLM reviews cannot substitute for human review or self-review.

You are allowed to generate LLM content that only you see, without disclosure, as long as you do not post it anywhere that you expect us to read or review.

Disclosure is required for machine translation, "trivial" changes, discovering bugs, and reviewing other people's work using an LLM. We welcome messages posted in your native language; English translation is not required to contribute.

There are very strict guidelines on LLM-generated code changes:

Pre-arranged, non-critical, high-quality, well-tested, and well-reviewed code changes that are originally created by an LLM are allowed, with disclosure.

The policy holds LLM-generated changes to a higher bar than human-authored changes, not a lower one: LLM PRs are required to have tests, full stop, regardless of how hard that is, as well as various other restrictions; LLMs must not generate soundness-critical changes unless the author is already a domain expert, and even then it's strongly discouraged.

In general, the policy focuses on understanding, helping to ensure that we have a mental model of our code, not just artifacts that mechanically do the right thing. Our motivation is influenced by Profession by Isaac Asimov. No programmer tapes.

Moderation rules

You must disclose LLM-generated content. You can choose to not post LLM content, or you can choose to post it and disclose its origin. You may not hide LLM involvement.

Harassment is not allowed. You may not harass people for using an LLM, regardless of whether or not their use is banned by the policy. You must follow the Code of Conduct at all times when interacting with the Rust project.

See the policy itself for more information.

Some parts of the policy are unenforceable. This is not a bug. The goal is not to catch every violation, but to create a clear bright-line rule: Disclosure is required for all public LLM text, unless specifically exempted by the policy. This allows moderators to identify violations based on actions, not on intent, and only consider intent when deciding how to respond.

How does this affect contributors?

Issue reporters

You must disclose any LLM involvement in discovering or reporting issues. You must tell us if you found an issue using an LLM. You must clearly quote and indicate which parts of your report were LLM-generated; the "no LLM-generated comments" rule applies to you too.

Authors who post LLM-generated code

I have written a list of guidelines you should follow if you make a PR to rust-lang/rust with LLM-generated code. You can avoid thinking about them, or indeed reading the list at all, if you follow this simple guideline from the policy:

It's fine to use LLMs to answer questions, analyze, distill, refine, check, suggest, review. But not to create.

See the "Allowed" section of the policy for a full list of what's meant by that. See rustc-dev-guide for the full list of guidelines.

Reviewers

General review

You are allowed to close PRs that don't follow the policy, no questions asked. Please point the author to #llm-mentoring at the same time. See the dev guide for exact circumstances and suggested wording.

You are not responsible for determining whether a PR is LLM-generated; that responsibility lies with the author. We will add a PR template that asks authors whether their code was LLM-generated so that this rarely comes up.

If an author claims their code is not LLM-generated, but you're still not sure, please report the PR privately to moderation. Style is not evidence; please do not accuse people of using an LLM. Reporting is not intended to be a penalty; the mod team is interested in seeing non-violations as well as violations.

Review of LLM code

If you have volunteered to review LLM PRs, the following section applies to you. No one is required to review LLM PRs unless they volunteer.

Everyone is expected to follow the new policy, not just authors. That means it is your responsibility to check whether an LLM-created PR touches an area that's disallowed by the policy, such as docs, diagnostics, or soundness-critical changes. You may request that the author redo it without LLM-generated code, in which case this section doesn't apply.

There's a more detailed summary of the rules you're expected to enforce in the dev guide. The official policy remains canonical.

What next?

Quite a lot of work has been put into this by moderators, team leads, reviewers, council representatives, and various other people inside and outside the project. Some of that work started months ago before the policy itself was written. I'd like to thank everyone who contributed, whether directly or indirectly.

This is not the end of the story. One of the goals of the policy is to help us gather data: Are people doing interesting and useful things with LLMs? Are they learning? Are they making repeat contributions? The answers to those questions will help us determine how the policy changes in the future.

This is not the first LLM policy published by teams in the Rust project, and hopefully it will not be the last. While the current policy only applies to the rust-lang/rust monorepo, I still believe that Rust would benefit from a project-wide policy that specifies what we expect in chats, forums, public communications, repositories without an explicit policy, and other cross-project areas.

sentences.en: Making code easier to write exacerbates our existing issues with review bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 让代码更容易编写会加剧我们现有的审查带宽问题。

blocks.html_en: • People mechanically copy-pasting to and from an LLM is a waste of our time.

sentences.en: People mechanically copy-pasting to and from an LLM is a waste of our time.
sentences.zh: 人们机械地在法学硕士之间进行复制粘贴是浪费我们的时间。

blocks.html_en: As time went on, these issues grew and grew, until we had to create dedicated channels and moderation policy for how to deal with them. However, those channels work against our goals of being transparent and welcoming, because new contributors have no idea what the rules are.

sentences.en: As time went on, these issues grew and grew, until we had to create dedicated channels and moderation policy for how to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这些问题越来越多，直到我们不得不创建专门的渠道和调节政策来处理它们。

sentences.en: However, those channels work against our goals of being transparent and welcoming, because new contributors have no idea what the rules are.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些渠道违背了我们透明和欢迎的目标，因为新的贡献者不知道规则是什么。

blocks.html_en: The new policy formalizes those rules publicly, so that new contributors know how to join our community without getting their PRs closed for reasons they don't understand, and so that existing reviewers can easily point to the rules as an actionable reason when closing PRs that don't follow them.

sentences.en: The new policy formalizes those rules publicly, so that new contributors know how to join our community without getting their PRs closed for reasons they don't understand, and so that existing reviewers can easily point to the rules as an actionable reason when closing PRs that don't follow them.
sentences.zh: 新政策公开正式化了这些规则，以便新的贡献者知道如何加入我们的社区，而不会因为他们不理解的原因而关闭他们的 PR，并且现有的审阅者可以在关闭不遵循规则的 PR 时轻松指出这些规则作为可行的原因。

blocks.html_en: Technical products no longer indicate effort

sentences.en: Technical products no longer indicate effort
sentences.zh: 技术产品不再代表努力

blocks.html_en: It used to be that if an open source project got a polished, well-tested, detailed PR, that indicated that there was someone on the other end who had put time, effort, and understanding into the PR. That influenced Rust's culture in several ways:

sentences.en: It used to be that if an open source project got a polished, well-tested, detailed PR, that indicated that there was someone on the other end who had put time, effort, and understanding into the PR.
sentences.zh: 过去，如果一个开源项目得到了一份精心设计、经过充分测试、详细的 PR，就表明另一端有人在 PR 中投入了时间、精力和理解。

sentences.en: That influenced Rust's culture in several ways:
sentences.zh: 这在几个方面影响了 Rust 的文化：

blocks.html_en: • We are generally reluctant to close PRs, since they represent someone else's hard work.

sentences.en: We are generally reluctant to close PRs, since they represent someone else's hard work.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不愿意关闭 PR，因为它们代表了其他人的辛勤工作。

blocks.html_en: • Our process emphasizes incremental discussions, where PRs are allowed to change existing design if we discover new facts during creation or review.

sentences.en: Our process emphasizes incremental discussions, where PRs are allowed to change existing design if we discover new facts during creation or review.
sentences.zh: 我们的流程强调渐进式讨论，如果我们在创建或审核过程中发现新事实，则允许 PR 更改现有设计。

blocks.html_en: • We treat PRs as an indication that someone is interested in joining our community and being mentored to work on future PRs.

sentences.en: We treat PRs as an indication that someone is interested in joining our community and being mentored to work on future PRs.
sentences.zh: 我们将 PR 视为有人有兴趣加入我们的社区并接受指导以开展未来 PR 的指示。

blocks.html_en: With LLMs, none of these signals are reliable. Polished PRs no longer indicate effort; authors of polished PRs no longer necessarily understand their code—and in the case of autonomous agents, there is no longer someone on the other end at all; and because it's become so much easier to write code, a polished PR no longer indicates that someone is likely to stick around for the long term.

sentences.en: With LLMs, none of these signals are reliable.
sentences.zh: 对于法学硕士来说，这些信号都不可靠。

sentences.en: Polished PRs no longer indicate effort; authors of polished PRs no longer necessarily understand their code—and in the case of autonomous agents, there is no longer someone on the other end at all; and because it's become so much easier to write code, a polished PR no longer indicates that someone is likely to stick around for the long term.
sentences.zh: 精美的 PR 不再表明努力；精心设计的 PR 的作者不再需要理解他们的代码——对于自主代理来说，另一端根本就不再有人了；而且由于编写代码变得更加容易，完美的 PR 不再表明某人可能会长期坚持下去。

blocks.html_en: Making code easier to write causes review issues

sentences.en: Making code easier to write causes review issues
sentences.zh: 让代码更容易编写会导致审查问题

blocks.html_en: At the time of writing, there are 1,281 open PRs to rust-lang/rust. This represents a staggering amount of time invested by both authors and reviewers. We have long had the problem that there are more people who want to write code than people willing to review it. With the advent of LLMs, this problem only gets worse.

sentences.en: At the time of writing, there are 1,281 open PRs to rust-lang/rust.
sentences.zh: 截至撰写本文时，有 1,281 个 rust-lang/rust 的开放 PR。

sentences.en: This represents a staggering amount of time invested by both authors and reviewers.
sentences.zh: 这代表着作者和审稿人投入的大量时间。

sentences.en: We have long had the problem that there are more people who want to write code than people willing to review it.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，我们一直面临这样的问题：想要编写代码的人比愿意审查代码的人多。

sentences.en: With the advent of LLMs, this problem only gets worse.
sentences.zh: 随着法学硕士的出现，这个问题只会变得更糟。

blocks.html_en: Most of the work of reviewing is not simply catching bugs. A great deal of it is deciding whether this direction is a good approach, whether the PR is a good idea at all. In other words, reviewing is made of decisions.

sentences.en: Most of the work of reviewing is not simply catching bugs.
sentences.zh: 大部分的review工作并不是简单的抓bug。

sentences.en: A great deal of it is deciding whether this direction is a good approach, whether the PR is a good idea at all.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分是决定这个方向是否是一个好方法，公关是否是一个好主意。

sentences.en: In other words, reviewing is made of decisions.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，审查是由决定组成的。

blocks.html_en: "Shotgunning" PRs at reviewers incurs a high mental cost for them. I think most authors of LLM PRs believe that they are sincerely helping, but from our perspective, the code itself is the smallest and in some ways least important part of the change. We care much more about authors understanding what the code does, planning how it will change in the future, and deciding what it should look like. The code itself cannot help with any of those.

sentences.en: "Shotgunning" PRs at reviewers incurs a high mental cost for them.
sentences.zh: 对审稿人进行“散弹式”公关会给他们带来高昂的心理成本。

sentences.en: I think most authors of LLM PRs believe that they are sincerely helping, but from our perspective, the code itself is the smallest and in some ways least important part of the change.
sentences.zh: 我认为大多数 LLM PR 的作者都认为他们是真诚地提供帮助，但从我们的角度来看，代码本身是变革中最小的、在某些方面也是最不重要的部分。

sentences.en: We care much more about authors understanding what the code does, planning how it will change in the future, and deciding what it should look like.
sentences.zh: 我们更关心作者理解代码的用途，规划未来如何改变，并决定代码应该是什么样子。

sentences.en: The code itself cannot help with any of those.
sentences.zh: 代码本身无法帮助解决其中任何一个问题。

blocks.html_en: Mechanically copy-pasting LLM output is a waste of time

sentences.en: Mechanically copy-pasting LLM output is a waste of time
sentences.zh: 机械地复制粘贴LLM输出是浪费时间

blocks.html_en: We will often get people who respond to review comments by copy-pasting them into their LLM, then copy-pasting its response back onto GitHub. Bluntly: this is a waste of everyone's time. If we wanted an LLM's opinion, we could have asked it ourselves. We want to hear your thoughts, not a machine's.

sentences.en: We will often get people who respond to review comments by copy-pasting them into their LLM, then copy-pasting its response back onto GitHub.
sentences.zh: 我们经常会让人们通过将评论复制粘贴到他们的 LLM 中，然后将其回复复制粘贴回 GitHub 来回复评论评论。

sentences.en: Bluntly: this is a waste of everyone's time.
sentences.zh: 说白了：这是浪费大家的时间。

sentences.en: If we wanted an LLM's opinion, we could have asked it ourselves.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想要法学硕士的意见，我们可以自己询问。

sentences.en: We want to hear your thoughts, not a machine's.
sentences.zh: 我们想听听您的想法，而不是机器的想法。

blocks.html_en: Moreover, this is a breach of trust between the reviewer and the author. Our assumption when we review is that we're talking to a real person who wants to do their best work. Pasting LLM text creates suspicion: does the author actually care? Is there a person here at all?

sentences.en: Moreover, this is a breach of trust between the reviewer and the author.
sentences.zh: 而且，这违反了审稿人和作者之间的信任。

sentences.en: Our assumption when we review is that we're talking to a real person who wants to do their best work.
sentences.zh: 当我们进行审查时，我们的假设是我们正在与一个真正想要尽力而为的人交谈。

sentences.en: Pasting LLM text creates suspicion: does the author actually care?
sentences.zh: 粘贴 LLM 文本会引起怀疑：作者真的关心吗？

sentences.en: Is there a person here at all?
sentences.zh: 这里有人吗？

blocks.html_en: So why a policy?

sentences.en: So why a policy?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么要制定政策呢？

blocks.html_en: Before this policy, we had a "wild west" approach to moderation. We had dozens of LLM PRs; no disclosure rules; people trying to add risky MIR optimizations as their first PR; and people posting "Verification: git diff --check" in their PR description as if that did something. While we had something for moderators to point to in the form of "Empower reviewers to reject burdensome PRs", our enforcement was inconsistent and our rules were not published anywhere. In practice, the rule was "anything goes, as long as it's not obviously horrible". Compared to the previous situation, the new policy is both much more strict and much more clear.

sentences.en: Before this policy, we had a "wild west" approach to moderation.
sentences.zh: 在这项政策之前，我们采取的是“狂野西部”的节制方法。

sentences.en: We had dozens of LLM PRs; no disclosure rules; people trying to add risky MIR optimizations as their first PR; and people posting "Verification: git diff --check" in their PR description as if that did something.
sentences.zh: 我们有数十名法学硕士 PR；没有披露规则；人们试图添加有风险的 MIR 优化作为他们的第一个 PR；人们在 PR 描述中发布“验证：git diff --check”，就好像这做了什么一样。

sentences.en: While we had something for moderators to point to in the form of "Empower reviewers to reject burdensome PRs", our enforcement was inconsistent and our rules were not published anywhere.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们有一些东西可以让版主以“授权审核者拒绝繁琐的 PR”的形式指出，但我们的执行不一致，而且我们的规则没有在任何地方发布。

sentences.en: In practice, the rule was "anything goes, as long as it's not obviously horrible".
sentences.zh: 在实践中，规则是“任何事情都可以，只要不是明显可怕的”。

sentences.en: Compared to the previous situation, the new policy is both much more strict and much more clear.
sentences.zh: 与之前的情况相比，新政策不仅更加严格，而且更加明确。

blocks.html_en: Regardless of your opinions on whether LLMs are good, bad, or a secret third thing, they can no longer be ignored. Our choices are not "no policy" or "policy". Our choice is whether to have the policy be an unofficial list of moderation notes or something we stand by publicly.

sentences.en: Regardless of your opinions on whether LLMs are good, bad, or a secret third thing, they can no longer be ignored.
sentences.zh: 无论您对法学硕士是好、坏还是秘密的第三件事的看法如何，它们都不能再被忽视。

sentences.en: Our choices are not "no policy" or "policy".
sentences.zh: 我们的选择不是“无政策”或“有政策”。

sentences.en: Our choice is whether to have the policy be an unofficial list of moderation notes or something we stand by publicly.
sentences.zh: 我们的选择是让该政策成为非正式的审核说明列表，还是我们公开支持的政策。

blocks.html_en: Why not ban LLMs altogether, or allow any use of LLMs that we think are pro-social? Because Rust governance doesn't work that way. We do not have a benevolent dictator who can say "No LLM-generated content, whether it be code or prose." or "AI is a tool, just like other tools we use".

sentences.en: Why not ban LLMs altogether, or allow any use of LLMs that we think are pro-social?
sentences.zh: 为什么不完全禁止法学硕士，或允许任何我们认为有利于社会的法学硕士的使用？

sentences.en: Because Rust governance doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 因为 Rust 治理并不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: We do not have a benevolent dictator who can say "No LLM-generated content, whether it be code or prose."
sentences.zh: 我们没有一个仁慈的独裁者可以说“禁止LLM生成的内容，无论是代码还是散文”。

sentences.en: or "AI is a tool, just like other tools we use".
sentences.zh: 或“人工智能是一种工具，就像我们使用的其他工具一样”。

blocks.html_en: Rust operates by consensus. As the policy says:

sentences.en: Rust operates by consensus.
sentences.zh: Rust 通过共识来运作。

sentences.en: As the policy says:
sentences.zh: 正如政策所说：

blocks.html_en:
There is not a consensus within the Rust project—and likely never will be—about when/how/where it is acceptable to use AI-based tools. Many members of the Rust project and community find value in AI; many others feel that its negative impact on society and the climate are severe enough that no use is acceptable. Still others are working out their opinion.

Despite these differences, there are many values we all share:

  • Building a community of deep experts in our collective projects.
  • Building an inclusive community where all feel welcome and respected.

sentences.en: There is not a consensus within the Rust project—and likely never will be—about when/how/where it is acceptable to use AI-based tools.
sentences.zh: 关于何时/如何/在何处使用基于人工智能的工具是可以接受的，Rust 项目内部尚未达成共识，而且可能永远不会达成共识。

sentences.en: Many members of the Rust project and community find value in AI; many others feel that its negative impact on society and the climate are severe enough that no use is acceptable.
sentences.zh: Rust 项目和社区的许多成员都发现了人工智能的价值；许多其他人认为它对社会和气候的负面影响非常严重，任何使用都是不可接受的。

sentences.en: Still others are working out their opinion.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人正在研究他们的意见。

sentences.en: Despite these differences, there are many values we all share: Building a community of deep experts in our collective projects.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在这些差异，但我们都有许多共同的价值观：在我们的集体项目中建立一个由资深专家组成的社区。

sentences.en: Building an inclusive community where all feel welcome and respected.
sentences.zh: 建立一个包容性的社区，让所有人都感到受欢迎和尊重。

blocks.html_en: We want it to be possible to change the policy in the future. The policy has several provisions that make it easier to change than it was to originally adopt. The leadership council is also considering creating a sub-team that would handle LLM policy so we have fewer "nightmare" 30-person approval requirements.

sentences.en: We want it to be possible to change the policy in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们希望将来能够改变政策。

sentences.en: The policy has several provisions that make it easier to change than it was to originally adopt.
sentences.zh: 该政策有几项规定，使其比最初采用时更容易更改。

sentences.en: The leadership council is also considering creating a sub-team that would handle LLM policy so we have fewer "nightmare" 30-person approval requirements.

blocks.html_en: I do not think every rule in this policy is wholly good. I do think that writing our rules down is better than not writing them down, and that having a policy that everyone kinda dislikes pushes us to improve our governance structures.

sentences.en: I do not think every rule in this policy is wholly good.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这项政策中的每一条规则都是好的。

blocks.html_en: Uses in the first category are allowed, sometimes requiring disclosure. Uses in the second category are heavily restricted.

blocks.html_en: General rules

sentences.en: General rules
sentences.zh: 一般规则

blocks.html_en: No one except the author is required to read LLM output unless they choose to: LLM output isn't allowed in public docs, PR descriptions, or Github comments unless it's clearly marked; reviewers aren't required to look at LLM PRs if they don't want to.

sentences.en: No one except the author is required to read LLM output unless they choose to: LLM output isn't allowed in public docs, PR descriptions, or Github comments unless it's clearly marked; reviewers aren't required to look at LLM PRs if they don't want to.
sentences.zh: 除作者外，任何人都不需要阅读 LLM 输出，除非他们选择： 公共文档、PR 描述或 Github 评论中不允许使用 LLM 输出，除非明确标记；如果审稿人不愿意，则不需要查看 LLM PR。

blocks.html_en: No one is required to use LLMs to contribute to rust-lang/rust: policies must be written first for humans, and only summarized for machines; LLM reviews cannot substitute for human review or self-review.

sentences.en: No one is required to use LLMs to contribute to rust-lang/rust: policies must be written first for humans, and only summarized for machines; LLM reviews cannot substitute for human review or self-review.
sentences.zh: 不需要任何人使用 LLM 来为 rust-lang/rust 做出贡献：策略必须首先为人类编写，只为机器总结； LLM 评审不能替代人工评审或自我评审。

blocks.html_en: You are allowed to generate LLM content that only you see, without disclosure, as long as you do not post it anywhere that you expect us to read or review.

sentences.en: You are allowed to generate LLM content that only you see, without disclosure, as long as you do not post it anywhere that you expect us to read or review.
sentences.zh: 您可以生成只有您自己能看到的 LLM 内容，无需披露，只要您不将其发布到您希望我们阅读或审查的任何地方即可。

blocks.html_en: Disclosure is required for machine translation, "trivial" changes, discovering bugs, and reviewing other people's work using an LLM. We welcome messages posted in your native language; English translation is not required to contribute.

sentences.en: Disclosure is required for machine translation, "trivial" changes, discovering bugs, and reviewing other people's work using an LLM.

content_html_zh:
最近，Rust 项目中的五个团队采用了我最初编写的一项政策，管理在为 rust-lang/rust monorepo 做出贡献时如何使用大型语言模型。 值得注意的是，新政策并不是对 LLM 的官方立场，并且并不适用于 Rust 项目中的所有地方。 我写它是为了一个非常具体的目的，如下所述。

这篇文章讨论了我们为什么制定该政策、它的内容以及这将如何影响贡献者。

该政策影响以下人群：

  • 审查或审核 rust-lang/rust 上的 PR 的人。
  • 在 rust-lang/rust 上使用 LLM 生成的代码编写 PR 的人。
  • 使用 LLM 发现问题并将其发布到 rust-lang/rust 上的人。
  • 在 rust-lang/rust 上撰写直接引用 LLM 的问题或评论的人。

如果您不属于这些群体之一，则无需改变任何工作方式。

为什么制定这项政策？

虽然 Rust 项目是技术工件的集合，但它也是一个由共同构建、维护和扩展这些工件的人员组成的社区。 当我们谈论“为 Rust 项目做出贡献”时，我们部分指的是对这些工件的工作，但我们也指加入该社区并与已有的人员合作。

甚至在这项政策制定之前，人们就开始使用法学硕士来为 rust-lang/rust 做出贡献。 其中一些用途尊重我们的社区：将消息翻译成英语，以便人们可以用自己的母语起草它们；为 Rust 的新贡献者可能编写的代码片段找到不良诊断；分析 RFC，看看它们是否遗漏了对可能影响设计的语言其他部分的讨论。 其中一些用途（有时是无意的）却没有。

我发现法学硕士给我们的社区带来了三个主要问题：

  1. 精美的技术产品不再表明努力和理解。
  2. 让代码更容易编写会加剧我们现有的审查带宽问题。
  3. 人们机械地在法学硕士之间进行复制粘贴是浪费我们的时间。

随着时间的推移，这些问题越来越多，直到我们不得不创建专门的渠道和调节政策来处理它们。 然而，这些渠道违背了我们透明和欢迎的目标，因为新的贡献者不知道规则是什么。

新政策公开正式化了这些规则，以便新的贡献者知道如何加入我们的社区，而不会因为他们不理解的原因而关闭他们的 PR，并且现有的审阅者可以在关闭不遵循规则的 PR 时轻松指出这些规则作为可行的原因。

技术产品不再代表努力

过去，如果一个开源项目得到了一份精心设计、经过充分测试、详细的 PR，就表明另一端有人在 PR 中投入了时间、精力和理解。 这在几个方面影响了 Rust 的文化：

  • 我们通常不愿意关闭 PR，因为它们代表了其他人的辛勤工作。
  • 我们的流程强调渐进式讨论，如果我们在创建或审核过程中发现新事实，则允许 PR 更改现有设计。
  • 我们将 PR 视为有人有兴趣加入我们的社区并接受指导以开展未来 PR 的指示。

对于法学硕士来说，这些信号都不可靠。 精美的 PR 不再表明努力；精心设计的 PR 的作者不再需要理解他们的代码——对于自主代理来说，另一端根本就不再有人了；而且由于编写代码变得更加容易，完美的 PR 不再表明某人可能会长期坚持下去。

让代码更容易编写会导致审查问题

截至撰写本文时，有 1,281 个 rust-lang/rust 的开放 PR。 这代表着作者和审稿人投入的大量时间。 长期以来，我们一直面临这样的问题：想要编写代码的人比愿意审查代码的人多。 随着法学硕士的出现，这个问题只会变得更糟。

大部分的review工作并不是简单的抓bug。 其中很大一部分是决定这个方向是否是一个好方法，公关是否是一个好主意。 换句话说，审查是由决定组成的。

对审稿人进行“散弹式”公关会给他们带来高昂的心理成本。 我认为大多数 LLM PR 的作者都认为他们是真诚地提供帮助，但从我们的角度来看，代码本身是变革中最小的、在某些方面也是最不重要的部分。 我们更关心作者理解代码的用途，规划未来如何改变，并决定代码应该是什么样子。 代码本身无法帮助解决其中任何一个问题。

机械地复制粘贴LLM输出是浪费时间

我们经常会让人们通过将评论复制粘贴到他们的 LLM 中，然后将其回复复制粘贴回 GitHub 来回复评论评论。 说白了：这是浪费大家的时间。 如果我们想要法学硕士的意见，我们可以自己询问。 我们想听听您的想法，而不是机器的想法。

而且，这违反了审稿人和作者之间的信任。 当我们进行审查时，我们的假设是我们正在与一个真正想要尽力而为的人交谈。 粘贴 LLM 文本会引起怀疑：作者真的关心吗？ 这里有人吗？

那么为什么要制定政策呢？

在这项政策之前，我们采取的是“狂野西部”的节制方法。 我们有数十名法学硕士 PR；没有披露规则；人们试图添加有风险的 MIR 优化作为他们的第一个 PR；人们在 PR 描述中发布“验证：git diff --check”，就好像这做了什么一样。 虽然我们有一些东西可以让版主以“授权审核者拒绝繁琐的 PR”的形式指出，但我们的执行不一致，而且我们的规则没有在任何地方发布。 在实践中，规则是“任何事情都可以，只要不是明显可怕的”。 与之前的情况相比，新政策不仅更加严格，而且更加明确。

无论您对法学硕士是好、坏还是秘密的第三件事的看法如何，它们都不能再被忽视。 我们的选择不是“无政策”或“有政策”。 我们的选择是让该政策成为非正式的审核说明列表，还是我们公开支持的政策。

为什么不完全禁止法学硕士，或允许任何我们认为有利于社会的法学硕士的使用？ 因为 Rust 治理并不是这样运作的。 我们没有一个仁慈的独裁者可以说“禁止LLM生成的内容，无论是代码还是散文”。 或“人工智能是一种工具，就像我们使用的其他工具一样”。

Rust 通过共识来运作。 正如政策所说：

关于何时/如何/在何处使用基于人工智能的工具是可以接受的，Rust 项目内部尚未达成共识，而且可能永远不会达成共识。 Rust 项目和社区的许多成员都发现了人工智能的价值；许多其他人认为它对社会和气候的负面影响非常严重，任何使用都是不可接受的。 还有一些人正在研究他们的意见。 尽管存在这些差异，但我们都有许多共同的价值观：在我们的集体项目中建立一个由资深专家组成的社区。 建立一个包容性的社区，让所有人都感到受欢迎和尊重。

我们希望将来能够改变政策。 该政策有几项规定，使其比最初采用时更容易更改。 领导委员会还在考虑创建一个负责处理 LLM 政策的子团队，以便我们减少“噩梦”的 30 人批准要求。

我不认为这项政策中的每一条规则都是好的。 我确实认为写下我们的规则比不写下它们要好，并且制定每个人都有点不喜欢的政策会促使我们改善我们的治理结构。

政策怎么说？

该政策是这样总结的：

使用法学硕士来回答问题、分析、提炼、提炼、检查、建议、审查是可以的。 但不是去创造。

第一类用途是允许的，有时需要披露。 第二类的用途受到严格限制。

一般规则

除作者外，任何人都不需要阅读 LLM 输出，除非他们选择： 公共文档、PR 描述或 Github 评论中不允许使用 LLM 输出，除非明确标记；如果审稿人不愿意，则不需要查看 LLM PR。

不需要任何人使用 LLM 来为 rust-lang/rust 做出贡献：策略必须首先为人类编写，只为机器总结； LLM 评审不能替代人工评审或自我评审。

您可以生成只有您自己能看到的 LLM 内容，无需披露，只要您不将其发布到您希望我们阅读或审查的任何地方即可。

机器翻译、“微不足道”的更改、发现错误以及使用法学硕士审查其他人的工作都需要披露。 我们欢迎用您的母语发布消息；不需要英文翻译即可投稿。

对于 LLM 生成的代码更改有非常严格的准则：

允许对最初由法学硕士创建的预先安排的、非关键的、高质量的、经过充分测试和充分审查的代码进行更改，并进行披露。

该政策将 LLM 生成的更改设置为比人类编写的更改更高的标准，而不是更低的标准：LLM PR 需要进行测试，句号，无论有多难，以及各种其他限制；除非作者已经是领域专家，否则法学硕士不得产生对可靠性至关重要的更改，即使如此，也强烈建议不要这样做。

一般来说，该政策侧重于理解，帮助确保我们对代码有一个心理模型，而不仅仅是机械地做正确事情的工件。 我们的动机受到艾萨克·阿西莫夫的《职业》的影响。 没有编程器磁带。

审核规则

您必须披露法学硕士生成的内容。 您可以选择不发布 LLM 内容，也可以选择发布该内容并披露其来源。 您不得隐瞒法学硕士的参与。

不允许骚扰。 您不得骚扰使用法学硕士的人，无论政策是否禁止他们的使用。 与 Rust 项目交互时，您必须始终遵守行为准则。

请参阅政策本身以获取更多信息。

该政策的某些部分无法执行。 这不是一个错误。 目标不是抓住每一个违规行为，而是制定一条明确的明线规则：所有公共法学硕士文本都需要披露，除非政策明确豁免。 这使得主持人可以根据行为而不是意图来识别违规行为，并且在决定如何响应时仅考虑意图。

这对贡献者有何影响？

问题记者

您必须披露法学硕士参与发现或报告问题的情况。 如果您在使用法学硕士时发现问题，您必须告诉我们。 您必须清楚地引用并指出报告的哪些部分是法学硕士生成的； “不得由法学硕士生成评论”规则也适用于您。

发布 LLM 生成代码的作者

我写了一份指南列表，如果您使用 LLM 生成的代码向 rust-lang/rust 进行 PR，您应该遵循这些指南。 如果您遵循政策中的以下简单指南，您就可以避免考虑它们，甚至根本不阅读该列表：

使用法学硕士来回答问题、分析、提炼、提炼、检查、建议、审查是可以的。 但不是去创造。

有关其含义的完整列表，请参阅策略的“允许”部分。 请参阅 rustc-dev-guide 以获取完整的指南列表。

审稿人

一般审查

您可以关闭不遵守该政策的 PR，无需提出任何问题。 请同时指出作者#llm-mentoring。 有关具体情况和建议的措辞，请参阅开发指南。

您不负责确定 PR 是否是 LLM 生成的；该责任由作者承担。 我们将添加一个 PR 模板，询问作者他们的代码是否是 LLM 生成的，这样这种情况就很少出现。

如果作者声称他们的代码不是 LLM 生成的，但您仍然不确定，请私下报告 PR 以进行审核。 风格不是证据，而是证据。请不要指责人们使用法学硕士。 举报并不是为了惩罚；国防部团队希望看到非违规行为和违规行为。

LLM代码审查

如果您自愿审查 LLM PR，则以下部分适用于您。 除非他们自愿，否则没有人需要审查法学硕士 PR。

每个人都应该遵守新政策，而不仅仅是作者。 这意味着您有责任检查 LLM 创建的 PR 是否涉及政策不允许的领域，例如文档、诊断或健全性关键更改。 您可以要求作者在没有 LLM 生成的代码的情况下重做它，在这种情况下，本节不适用。

开发指南中提供了您需要执行的规则的更详细摘要。 官方政策仍然是规范的。

接下来怎么办？

主持人、团队领导、审阅者、理事会代表以及项目内外的其他各种人员为此投入了大量的工作。 其中一些工作在政策本身制定之前几个月就开始了。 我要感谢所有直接或间接做出贡献的人。

故事还没有结束。 该政策的目标之一是帮助我们收集数据：人们是否利用法学硕士做了有趣且有用的事情？ 他们在学习吗？ 他们是否重复做出贡献？ 这些问题的答案将帮助我们确定未来政策如何变化。

这不是 Rust 项目团队发布的第一个 LLM 政策，希望也不会是最后一个。 虽然当前的政策仅适用于 rust-lang/rust monorepo，但我仍然相信 Rust 将从项目范围的政策中受益，该政策指定了我们在聊天、论坛、公共通信、没有明确政策的存储库以及其他跨项目领域的期望。
